show_hn.title: Show HN: Musql, JIT-compiled SQL, up to 300x faster than SQLite, 1000x vs. Turso
show_hn.story_text: Howdy HN! Missing a fast pure Go embedded SQL database. The issue is that compared to C, go is slow. Having done a lot of JIT in go, I naturally wanted to stick a JIT that generates native query kernels and see what happens. Result: musql. Pronounced "muscle." On a 100K-row filtered count, musql takes 21 µs: about 300x faster than C SQLite and nearly 1,000x faster than Turso. Single-threaded, warm cache, using musql's direct API, native C SQLite, and Turso's Go driver. Filtered sums are 130x faster than C SQLite, grouped aggregates 95x. It works with Go's database/sql or through a server for libSQL clients. It uses its own storage format, with SQLite import/export. And yes, the SQL VM runs DOOM.     conv in.mp4 out.gif
and you get your GIF from the right tool (ffmpeg, ImageMagick, etc.) using settings tuned for good output. And if you've ever had an issue uploading a file that is too large, you can use the --max-size flag: 
    conv clip.mp4 --max-size 10mb

show_hn.title: Show HN: POSIX-UEFI
show_hn.story_text: Dependency-free POSIX compatibility layer and build environment for UEFI. https://gitlab.com/bztsrc/posix-uefi Its goal is twofold: provides the usual libc API for EFI applications and an SDK on POSIX systems to create such EFI applications with a build system that works with CLang and gcc as well. Its API is nowhere near complete as GNU-EFI's or EDKII's, so it provides seamless integration with those headers to make the API expandable. It is also not a fully POSIX standard compatible libc, it's just a wrapper around the firmware provided features with some minimal additions, but provides enough for everyday use cases.
